title: Thor Henning Hetland
description: Software architect, AI development pioneer, founder of JavaZone and eXOReaction

items.title: Hiring by the Book: A Defendable HR Agent on a Regulatory Knowledge Web
items.content_html: Can we use an AI tool to screen job applicants? Every organization is asking; almost none can defend the answer. We wire a customer's HR agent to Mynder's regulatory knowledge web through kcp-agent's MCP bridge — and the first plan we ran was wrong, which turns out to be the strongest argument for the architecture. A working blueprint for regulated agentic knowledge work, plus the red-team list of what's still missing.

items.title: The Borrowed Leash: Determinism as a Service for the Agentic Web
items.content_html: kcp-agent 0.3.0 turns deterministic knowledge navigation into a service any MCP-capable agent can borrow. Your agent doesn't have to become deterministic — it just has to ask someone who is. What the KCP/MCP bridge uncovers for the agentic web: identity and economics across process boundaries, evidence that survives cross-examination, and governance that lives in one place instead of N system prompts.

items.title: The Vibes-Based Agent Era Deserves to End
items.content_html: kcp-agent 0.2.0 ships — and it's an argument, not just a release. The industry builds agents where the model decides everything: unreproducible, unauditable, injectable. This is the inversion: determinism at the core, the LLM at the edge, every decision defensible. The vibes-based agent era has a working counter-example now.

items.title: Selling News to Robots
items.content_html: KCP v0.25 promotes RFC-0005 — the economic metadata layer. A step-by-step how-to: build a paid-for news service for agents, then watch an agent with a funded wallet window-shop five candidate articles, buy two, and walk away with receipts.

items.title: One Agent's Journey Through the Whole Protocol
items.content_html: v0.24 shipped today — the enterprise front door. Twenty-four versions in six months, and every layer now has a job: discovery, meaning, trust, time, identity, federation. One agent's traversal through the whole protocol, annotated.

items.title: The Agentic Web Has No Login Page
items.content_html: The agentic web has no login page — so the only knowledge agents can consume is what publishers give away. KCP v0.22 and v0.23 add the missing half of the trust model: who may consume knowledge, and how they prove it.

items.title: The Third Test Harness
items.content_html: Unit tests catch logic bugs. Integration tests catch assembly bugs. The third harness catches specification drift — and it's the one AI-augmented teams need most.

items.title: The CI Pipeline Is the Agent's Nervous System
items.content_html: When the agent writes code that passes locally but fails in CI, it's not a test problem. It's a nervous system problem.

items.title: Against the Swarm
items.content_html: The industry is building swarms of competing agents. The value is in one agent that knows your work.

items.title: Three Hooks That Give Claude Code Memory
items.content_html: Three passive hooks that give Claude Code memory, routing, and hygiene — without changing how you work. The session amnesia problem, and how to fix it at the prompt boundary.

items.title: Cloud Computing: Are You Looking for IaaS or PaaS Provider?
items.content_html: Comparing IaaS and PaaS cloud models from Amazon, Google, and Microsoft -- and why the choice between platform and infrastructure shapes everything.

items.title: Clouded Vision
items.content_html: Cloud savings come from zero-admin architecture, not cheaper servers. Most apps carry enterprise DNA that makes migration painful without rethinking the design.

items.title: Open Source and Community Clouds
items.content_html: Early open-source cloud platforms StratusLab and Eucalyptus offered EC2-compatible infrastructure on your own hardware, with real management challenges.

items.title: Sinnataggen and some Cloud development thoughts...
items.content_html: Gartner's six criteria for evaluating cloud development platforms, from interoperability and mobile support to vendor longevity and ecosystem quality.

items.title: Trouble In The Clouds - Gmail Turns Into Gfail
items.content_html: Gmail's February 2009 outage exposed cloud reliability gaps and Google's slow communication -- three hours before acknowledging a widespread service failure.

items.title: Why clouds should be more like operating systems
items.content_html: Managing multiple AMIs still requires manual sysadmin. Clouds need dashboard tooling and automated administration to deliver on their promise.

items.title: Its time for auto scaling - avoid peak load provisioning for web applications
items.content_html: Applications cannot use new compute resources dynamically without middleware virtualisation. Auto-scaling requires architecture, not just infrastructure.

items.title: Cloud - auto-magic or just provisioning platform for your distributed system
items.content_html: Clouds are provisioning platforms, not silver bullets. Enterprises still want magic, but the real question is whether to educate or go with the flow.

items.title: Gartner on Cloud Computing, misses again...
items.content_html: Gartner's five cloud attributes conflate delivery models, deployment models, and key characteristics into a flat taxonomy that obscures more than it reveals.

items.title: On the greenness of Clouds
items.content_html: Cloud computing is greener than in-house servers today, but componentisation drives consumption. If computation gets too cheap to measure, waste will follow.
